chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Yahya ibn Imran al-Hamedany, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, on the authority of Umar ibn Yazid, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'It has reached us that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand gates, each of which opens one thousand gates?'
He said: 'Yes.' [Then he said to me: 'Rather, He taught him a single gate, and that gate opened one thousand gates, and each of those gates opened one thousand gates.']
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the 'one thousand gates' and the 'single gate' taught to Ali by the Prophet?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to highlight the concept of *al-Bab al-Ahad* (the One Gate), suggesting that Ali (AS) received a singular, comprehensive principle of divine wisdom from which all other knowledge emanates. This correction from 'a thousand gates' to 'one gate opening to a thousand' underscores the Shia belief in the unity and depth of the Imam's knowledge, where a single foundational truth unlocks infinite layers of understanding. It reflects the scholarly view that the Prophet’s teaching to Ali was not merely a collection of facts but a holistic system of *Hikmah* (wisdom).
